title: From Individual Improvisation to Collective Heuristics: Modeling Adaptive Disability Instruction as Distributed Practice in Resource-Limited Indonesian Inclusive Schools
content: Background: Teachers in resource-limited Indonesian inclusive schools routinely meet disability-related instructional challenges through improvisation, yet research continues to treat such adaptive practice as an individual cognitive attribute, detached from the social and material conditions that sustain it. Purpose: This study reconceptualizes adaptive disability instruction as a collectively distributed, narratively co-constructed, and dynamically stabilized network of heuristics, and proposes the Participatory Critical-Incident and Distributed-Cognition Adaptive Practice System (PC-DC APS) for studying it. Method: The five-module framework elicits critical incidents through structured narrative interviews and collaborative debriefs, codifies them into adaptive pathways through multilingual embedding and iterative thematic clustering, maps a socio-material interaction graph through ethnographic shadowing and experience sampling, models heuristic stabilization as diffusion over a mentorship subgraph, and integrates these outputs in a dynamic structural equation model. The framework was applied to 412 critical incidents from 68 teachers in nine rural schools across three districts. Findings: Seven coherent adaptive pathways emerged, with material improvisation the most frequently instantiated. Informal mentors, mainly experienced teachers and community health workers rather than principals, occupied the most central network positions and conditioned which heuristics became entrenched. The dynamic model fitted the data adequately (CFI = 0.941, TLI = 0.927, RMSEA = 0.048), and its non-recursive feedback paths raised the explained variance in student engagement from 0.46 to 0.58 relative to a static model. Contribution: Rather than relying on static belief surveys and unvalidated trial-and-error constructs, the framework offers a substitution chain of measurable representations of collective practice, giving inclusive-education research a methodological backbone for capturing context-sensitive adaptive expertise as it is produced, shared, and sustained in resource-limited school communities.
